task.description:
This combines WF-03 Step 0.5 (registry lookup) and Step 1 (diagnose) for ISS-0423. Read docs/issues/ISS-0423.yaml in full, including its 'Re-opened for a second pass' note at the bottom -- it already reconciles most of this for you: ISS-0427 (template-schema clone), ISS-0428 (wire scripts/test_parallel.sh into mix letflow.check) and ISS-0426 (parallel wall-clock flake) are all status: resolved; ISS-0113 (Letflow.TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 calling Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto) globally) is still status: open and is this record's own named root cause of why 86+ already-async:-true test files still ran serially.

Do NOT re-derive the historical measurement work already in the file (measured_causes, adoption_notes) -- treat it as Step 0.5's registry-lookup match, already found for you. Your job is:

1. RE-VERIFY THE CURRENT BASELINE FIRST-HAND. Run the actual current gate command a real WF-02/WF-03 run would hit: `mix letflow.check` (this now shells to scripts/test_parallel.sh per ISS-0428 -- confirm this yourself by reading lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex, don't take the note's word for it) and ALSO a plain, un-partitioned `mix test` for a true serial baseline comparable to the original 2026-09-02 filing. Quote both 'Finished in ... (Xs async, Ys sync)' lines verbatim, real output, not estimated. This is the single most load-bearing thing this step produces: the queue task's own '~30 min gate on every requirement' framing may already be stale now that mix letflow.check parallelizes by default -- state plainly whether it still is or isn't a ~30 min gate today.
2. Confirm the CURRENT shape of the tenant fixture against ISS-0423's original description: is TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 still defaulting to template:clone (ISS-0427)? Count current async:true test files and current serial async:Xs from the real run in step 1 (not the stale '86 files / 14.8s' figures) -- has ISS-0113's defeat of async actually changed since 2026-09-02, or does the same global Sandbox.mode(:auto) call still block it? Read test/support/tenant_fixture.ex yourself to confirm the call site and line.
3. Read docs/issues/ISS-0113.yaml in full -- what does IT already scope as the fix (restoring :manual, or scoping :auto per-test)? Does fixing ISS-0113 first change the async picture, or does it just fix ISS-0113's own named correctness hazard without unlocking speed?
4. Root-cause diagnosis, written into result.summary: given the CURRENT state (ISS-0427/0428/0426 resolved, ISS-0113 open, mix letflow.check already parallelized), what is the real remaining opportunity for ISS-0423, if any? Is it: (a) fixing ISS-0113 to unlock the already-declared async:true files, (b) a SandboxPool-backed fixture rework to let MORE files go async (the pool-of-pre-provisioned-schemas idea the issue originally suggested), (c) something else, or (d) a reasoned finding that the remaining gap is not worth closing given what's already landed? State which, with the fresh measurement backing it. You are NOT implementing anything -- this is diagnosis for CODE-DESIGNER.
5. Read docs/migration/decisions/0009-test-parallel-pool-sizing.md in full (its addendum too) before finishing -- your diagnosis must state explicitly whether whatever you're recommending CODE-DESIGNER design interacts with the pool_size arithmetic that decision governs (peak concurrent DBConnection checkouts vs pool_size), even if only to say 'not applicable because X'.

Complete this handoff with next_action pointing at CODE-DESIGNER for fix/improvement design, UNLESS your finding is itself a complete, evidence-backed 'nothing further worth doing' verdict -- in which case say so plainly and route back to ORCH for a no-code-change closure discussion (AC6 of the queue task's own acceptance criteria explicitly allows this outcome).
acceptance_criteria: Both a fresh mix letflow.check run and a fresh plain mix test run are executed for real in this session and their exact 'Finished in ... (Xs async, Ys sync)' lines are quoted verbatim in result.summary

The current line number and exact call in test/support/tenant_fixture.ex responsible for the global Sandbox.mode(:auto) call is re-confirmed by reading the file, not assumed from ISS-0113's filing text
ISS-0113.yaml is read in full and its own proposed fix (if any) is summarized
A root-cause diagnosis is written stating which of (a)/(b)/(c)/(d) above this run should pursue, with the fresh measurement as evidence
Decision 0009 (plus its ISS-0287 addendum) is read in full and explicitly addressed in the diagnosis, even if only to state non-applicability with a reason
No fix is implemented in this step -- diagnosis only

result.summary:
FRESH MEASUREMENTS (this session, this host, 2026-09-05, real runs, exit code and full log inspected for each):

1) Plain serial `mix test`: 'Finished in 1316.3 seconds (18.2s async, 1298.1s sync)'. 'Result: 3227 passed (6 properties, 3221 tests), 21 excluded'. 0 failures. This is the true serial baseline comparable to ISS-0423's original 2026-09-02 filing (1805.1s) -- down ~27% purely from ISS-0427's template-clone landing (no test-count regression: 3221 vs 3054 tests then, suite has grown).

2) `mix letflow.check` / `mix letflow.check.test` (shells to scripts/test_parallel.sh per ISS-0428, confirmed by reading lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex:125-135 `run_main_suite/0` -> `stream_and_capture(bash, ["scripts/test_parallel.sh"])`): FAILED, reproducibly, twice in a row on this host. `test_parallel: N=16 (source: nproc)`, `TEST_POOL_SIZE=5`. Partitions 9-16 (the second half) crash identically both runs: `** (Postgrex.Error) ERROR 42P07 (duplicate_table) relation "secrets" already exists` during ecto.create/migrate at partition startup, before any test runs. `combined: 1549 tests, 4 properties, 0 failures (1553/1553 passed)` from only the 8 surviving partitions -- so no 'Finished in ... (Xs async, Ys sync)' line exists for this path at all today; the run never reaches ExUnit. This is the ISS-0219/ISS-0222 class already on record ('over-provisioning N relative to the host's CPU/Postgres budget crashes partitions outright at ecto.create/migrate time') -- not a new defect, but current, reproducible evidence that N=16 (this host's nproc-derived default) is NOT safely usable here today, contradicting the comfortable assumption that ISS-0428's landing made `mix letflow.check` a reliable fast path everywhere. I also attempted TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 to get a clean parallel timing figure; that run hung for >20 minutes with zero Postgres activity (confirmed via `pg_stat_activity` and `docker stats` showing 0% CPU) before I killed the stray erl.exe process -- I did not re-attempt a third parallel configuration given diagnosis-only scope and time already spent; a real 'Xs async, Ys sync' line for a clean parallel run is NOT available from this session on this host, only ISS-0428's own already-recorded figures (serial 1466s / N=2 774s / N=16 ~300s, and CI's real N=4 in ~5min) which I am not fabricating as if freshly measured.

STALENESS OF THE QUEUE TASK'S OWN '~30 min gate' FRAMING: partially stale, partially still true, and worth stating precisely rather than picking one side. `mix letflow.check` does NOT parallelize reliably by default on every host -- on THIS host, today, it fails outright at N=16 before producing any test result, which is arguably worse than a slow-but-working ~22min (1316s) serial gate. Where it does work (CI's N=4, ISS-0428's own figures), it is genuinely no longer a ~30min gate. So: 'no longer a reliable universal ~30min gate' is accurate; 'reliably fast now' is not -- it is host-dependent and this host currently regresses to failure, not to slow-but-safe serial.

3) test/support/tenant_fixture.ex current shape: `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :auto)` is still called, unconditionally and unrestored, at line 206 inside `provisioned_tenant!/1` (confirmed by direct read, not inherited from ISS-0113's older line-171 comment reference which is prose in the moduledoc, not the call site). `opts[:template]` defaults to `:clone` (line 212, `Keyword.get(opts, :template, :clone)`) -- ISS-0427 fully landed and is live for every caller by default. TenantFixture/provisioned_tenant! adoption has grown to 87 files (grep, up from ISS-0423's original 46); 93 files now declare `async: true` (up from 86). Despite that growth, async is STILL almost entirely defeated: 18.2s of 1316.3s = 1.4% async share in today's fresh run, essentially unchanged in kind from the original 14.8s/1805.1s = 0.8%. ISS-0427 (template speed) and ISS-0428 (parallel wiring) are both real, orthogonal wins; NEITHER touched this line or the async-defeat mechanism at all. ISS-0113 remains the sole, unremoved, still-active root cause of async defeat.

4) ISS-0113.yaml read in full. It documents one CONCRETE ATTEMPTED FIX (2026-08-21, WF03-ISS0113-20260821) that was tried for real and reverted: adding `Sandbox.mode(Letflow.Repo, :manual)` + a fresh `Sandbox.checkout(Letflow.Repo)` at the end of `provisioned_tenant!/1`, restoring the pre-fixture mode. Measured result: 125/125 baseline -> 113/125 with the fix, 12 failures across THREE distinct, independently-real mechanisms: (a) a test that itself later calls `Sandbox.checkout/1` expecting `:ok` under ambient `:auto` mode, now getting `{:already, :owner}`; (b) tests that deliberately spawn a second process to hold a real FOR UPDATE lock concurrently, which needs genuine multi-process access to the real pool, impossible under a single-owner sandboxed connection; (c) tests that call `TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema!`/`replay_migrations!` a SECOND time within the same test body, which itself requires `:auto` mode to let Ecto.Migrator's own connection checkout succeed. ISS-0113's own conclusion: a BLANKET restore-to-:manual inside the shared fixture is unsafe -- it must be a PER-CALLER OPT-IN (e.g. `opts[:restore_sandbox]`, default `false` i.e. unchanged), not a global default, and doing this correctly is squarely ISS-0112's territory (the 41-site fixture-consolidation issue) because each of the 87 current call sites needs individual verification against these three failure mechanisms before being flipped to opt in. ISS-0113 does NOT propose a SandboxPool-backed rework itself -- that idea belongs to ISS-0423/ISS-0427's own text, not ISS-0113.

ROOT-CAUSE DIAGNOSIS -- which of (a)/(b)/(c)/(d): (a), qualified. Fixing ISS-0113 (per-caller opt-in restore, scoped correctly per its own investigation notes) is the only remaining lever this record's own causal chain identifies that could unlock the 87 already-`async: true`-declared TenantFixture call sites' real async execution -- there is no other blocker on record between 'file says async: true' and 'test actually runs concurrently'; the global `Sandbox.mode(:auto)` at tenant_fixture.ex:206 is structurally exactly what defeats it, confirmed both by direct code read and by the fresh 1.4%-async measurement. (b), a SandboxPool-backed fixture rework for MORE async coverage (beyond what's already declared), is a materially larger, separate lever -- Letflow.SandboxPool already exists and is quota-bounded/claim-release-shaped for exactly this, but adopting it as TenantFixture's backing store is a new provisioning-strategy design, not a fix to the one line already blocking today's declared-but-inert async files. I recommend CODE-DESIGNER scope (a) first (fix ISS-0113 properly, i.e. design the per-caller opt-in and the migration plan across the 87 sites, explicitly building on ISS-0113's own three documented failure mechanisms rather than re-discovering them) and treat (b) as an explicitly out-of-scope follow-on to file separately if (a)'s real speedup turns out to leave a large remaining gap -- this mirrors exactly how ISS-0427 was split out from this same issue previously, and avoids re-committing the same 'one issue tries to do two levers' mistake this record's own history already shows was corrected twice. (d) 'nothing further worth doing' is NOT the right call: 1.4% async share against 93 declared-async files is a real, measured, unclosed gap, not a diminishing-returns situation.

DECISION 0009 (+ISS-0287 addendum) RECONCILIATION: 0009 governs `N * TEST_POOL_SIZE` vs Postgres `max_connections` for scripts/test_parallel.sh's cross-partition arithmetic. Fixing ISS-0113 (recommendation (a)) does NOT touch N, TEST_POOL_SIZE, or partition count at all -- it changes what happens to ONE already-checked-out connection's sandbox mode WITHIN a single test process, strictly inside whatever pool_size that test's own partition (or the plain non-partitioned `mix test` case) already has. It does, however, interact with a DIFFERENT, per-partition-internal quantity 0009 does not govern: PEAK CONCURRENT DBConnection CHECKOUTS WITHIN one partition's own Ecto pool. Today, with `async: true` defeated, at most one test per partition genuinely holds a checkout at a time regardless of how many files declare async (ExUnit still schedules them, but the shared `:auto` mode serializes real DB access in practice via the fixture's own behavior). If ISS-0113's fix genuinely unlocks concurrent async execution across the 87 sites, peak concurrent checkouts per partition could rise from ~1 toward however many async test processes ExUnit schedules at once (default: number of schedulers), which COULD exceed a partition's own `TEST_POOL_SIZE` (5 at N=16 on this host, 21 at N=4) -- this is the same class of hazard 0009/ISS-0287 already solved for the N-way cross-partition case, but recurring one level down, inside a single partition, which 0009's own formula does not account for at all (0009's `budget/N` computes pool size assuming each partition's OWN internal concurrency stays low). CODE-DESIGNER must size this explicitly: either confirm ExUnit's own `--max-cases`/scheduler-derived concurrency stays under whatever TEST_POOL_SIZE a partition gets, or have the ISS-0113 fix design cap it. This is NOT a reason to block the fix, but it is a real sizing question 0009 raises and does not answer, and must be addressed in the design rather than discovered later as a new connection-exhaustion issue the way ISS-0287 was discovered after 0009 shipped.

SECONDARY FINDING, in scope for CODE-DESIGNER's awareness but not this issue's own AC: the reproducible N=16 `mix letflow.check.test` failure on this host (partitions 9-16 crashing on `secrets` duplicate_table) is real, current, and would make `mix letflow.check` an unreliable gate on hosts like this one today, independent of anything in this diagnosis. It is the ISS-0219/ISS-0222 class already on record, not a new issue, and is being reported here rather than filed fresh since ISS-0423's own task explicitly asked whether the '~30min gate' framing is stale -- part of the honest answer is that on this host, it is not merely slow, it currently fails.

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER: design a fix for ISS-0113 (per-caller opt-in Sandbox mode restore in Letflow.TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1, per its own investigation notes distinguishing the three failure mechanisms already found) as the mechanism to unlock real async:true execution for the 87 current TenantFixture call sites. Design must explicitly address the peak-concurrent-DBConnection-checkout sizing question raised above against decision 0009/ISS-0287's TEST_POOL_SIZE arithmetic (a new per-partition-internal concern, not the cross-partition N*pool_size concern 0009 already governs). A SandboxPool-backed fixture rework (broader lever, beyond currently-declared async: true files) should be scoped as an explicit follow-on issue if the ISS-0113 fix's real measured speedup leaves a large gap, not folded into the same design.
